description: Capsicum annuum, hot types: a bushy plant with slender, pungent fruit.

diseases.name: Chilli Leaf Curl
diseases.pathogen: Chilli leaf curl virus and other begomoviruses
diseases.description: The most damaging virus disease of chilli: leaves curl, pucker and shrink, and the plant stops growing.
diseases.causes: Whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci) carry the virus from infected plants and weeds as they feed.
symptoms: Leaves curl upward and inward, puckered and thickened
Young leaves small, pale and crowded at the tips
Plants stunted, with few flowers and fruit
diseases.untreated: Early infection can make a whole planting worthless.

steps.title: Remove infected plants early
steps.instruction: Pull out curled, stunted plants and bag them.
steps.rationale: Each one is a source for whiteflies.

steps.title: Keep whiteflies off
steps.instruction: Use insect netting on seedlings, yellow sticky traps, and controls registered locally.

steps.title: Remove weed hosts
steps.rationale: Weeds harbour the virus and whiteflies.

prevention.title: Raise seedlings under netting
prevention.detail: Early infection is the most damaging.

lifecycle: Whiteflies pick up the virus from infected plants.
They carry it to healthy plants.
New leaves curl, pucker and shrink.
The plant stops growing and sets little fruit.

diseases.name: Anthracnose (Fruit Rot)
diseases.description: A fungal rot of chilli fruit, also called die back when it kills the shoot tips.
diseases.causes: Spores come in on seed and debris and spread by rain splash in warm, wet weather, mostly on ripening fruit.
symptoms: Round, sunken, water-soaked spots on ripening fruit
Concentric rings of dark dots or orange spore masses in the spots
Shoot tips die back from the top
diseases.effect: Rotting fruit is lost before and after harvest.
diseases.untreated: Can destroy much of a crop in wet seasons.

steps.title: Remove rotting fruit and dead shoot tips
steps.instruction: Pick off rotting fruit and dead shoot tips when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide from fruit set on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

prevention.title: Remove crop debris
prevention.detail: Rotate away from chilli for 2-3 years.

lifecycle: The fungus survives on seed and debris.
Rain splashes spores onto ripening fruit.
Sunken spots with rings of spores form.
Rotting fruit spreads it to its neighbours.

diseases.name: Cercospora Leaf Spot
diseases.description: A fungal leaf spot of chilli with pale-centred, dark-ringed 'frog-eye' spots.
diseases.causes: Spores survive on debris and seed and spread by wind and rain in warm, humid weather.
symptoms: Round spots with light grey centres
A dark brown ring round each spot
diseases.effect: Leaf drop exposes fruit to sunscald and cuts yield.

steps.title: Remove spotted leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off spotted leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

prevention.title: Rotate crops
prevention.detail: Two years away from chilli and pepper.

lifecycle: The fungus survives on debris and seed.
Wind and splash carry spores to leaves.
Grey-centred spots with dark rings form.
Leaves drop and spores spread.

diseases.name: Powdery Mildew
diseases.description: A powdery mildew that grows inside chilli leaves: white powder underneath, yellow patches on top.
diseases.causes: Spores blow on the wind; warm days, cool nights and dry leaves favour it.
symptoms: Pale yellow patches on the upper leaf
White to grey powdery growth on the underside
diseases.effect: Heavy leaf drop cuts yield and causes sunscald.

steps.title: Remove badly affected leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off badly affected leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Improve airflow
steps.rationale: Shade and still air favour mildew.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray sulphur or another registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: Spores blow in from infected plants.
They infect the leaves from below.
Yellow patches show on top, white powder under.
Leaves drop as it spreads.

diseases.name: Whitefly
diseases.description: Tiny white sap-sucking insects under chilli leaves; they also spread leaf curl virus.
diseases.causes: Whiteflies breed fast in warm, dry weather and fly between crops and weeds.
symptoms: Clouds of tiny white insects fly up when the plant is shaken
Yellow speckling and yellowing of the leaves
Sticky honeydew and black sooty mould on lower leaves
diseases.effect: Feeding weakens plants; honeydew and sooty mould soil the leaves.
diseases.untreated: They spread leaf curl virus, which is worse than the feeding.

steps.title: Check leaf undersides
steps.instruction: Count whiteflies and nymphs under the leaves.
steps.rationale: Shows how heavy the infestation is.

steps.title: Control if numbers are high
steps.instruction: Use a control registered locally (soap or oil sprays where advised), following the label.

lifecycle: Whiteflies fly in from weeds and other crops.
They feed and lay eggs under the leaves.
Leaves speckle yellow; honeydew collects.
Numbers explode in warm, dry weather.
